name: Gorgon

attributes.attribute: male sacred head found in the temple of Sulis
Greek goddess whose severed head became a Roman warning sign
local sun goddess of the hot springs at Bath
a fusion of Greek, Roman, and Celtic meanings

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The Greek gorgon Medusa was a goddess whose severed head the Romans reused as a warning sign. When Roman troops reached Celtic lands, they met an older head cult. The Celtic sacred head was usually male, not female. So the male gorgon carved in the temple of Sulis at Bath blends Greek, Roman, and Celtic meanings into a single image. Sulis was the local sun goddess of that hot-spring shrine.

okr.objective: Explain the male Celtic gorgon head in contrast to the female Greek Medusa and the Sulis find-site.
key_results: The Celtic sacred head was typically male, unlike the goddess Medusa.
The male gorgon was found in the temple of Sulis at Bath.
